comments.author: @cochinaable
comments.text:
Sadly the influx of American retirees to Dumaguete has made life difficult for the locals. The prices of rent, land, food, restaurants and now domestic helpers have gone up making it unaffordable or steeper for the locals. On top of that 'most' American retirees, who we locals refer to as 'economic refugees' are arrogant, demanding, entitled and abrasive.  Yes. Some are pleasant many are tolerable but most are downright abusive to locals and demand that we adapt to their 'civilized' lifestyle instead of them adjusting to our culture.
Growing up my grandparents who experienced life under the colonial rule of the Americans, told us there were different kinds of Americans... the good, the bad and the ugly. I have long  realized what they mean.
Filipinos are generally hospitable and extremely tolerant but it's not infinite. Push too far and it will break and it has.
I've been all over the world and all over the USA and I've experienced racism the worst was in America. But what really is abhorrent is for a Filipino to be discriminated in his own country by an 'economic refugee'.

comments.author: @MikeFoulks-t8x
comments.text: I've called this place home for the last 6 months. The video is pretty accurate. Poverty is still a part of life here, but much more hidden than in places like Cebu or Manila.  It is a very friendly city. I have a comfortable, fairly modern apartment along a dirt road by the ocean for under $300/month after figuring in utilities. I spend another $300/month for food because I typically dine out. I ride around on a scooter, which uses about $100/month in gasoline because I ride around a lot. I don't need medical care yet, so the rest of my budget is just discretionary spending. I'm not retired, so I will have to return to the US at some point, but I will miss this place dearly. I can definitely see myself retiring here as long as I'm healthy when that time comes.
